title: Interview candidate: hikikomorphism (@hikikomorphism.bsky.social), who posted a cyberdeck design and security advisories found by property testing, and answered questions about both
summary: hikikomorphism (5,508 followers) wrote 311 posts in the window, most of them replies. Two things she made are in it. Through the week she posted GitHub security advisories credited to her in open-source projects, found by a property-testing pipeline run with coding agents, with the line "today's reminder to property test your codebase before someone else does it for you" (16 Nov, 98 likes); another member reported fixing about 60 bugs with the method. On 19 Nov she posted a first draft of a custom cyberdeck (105 likes, with an image) and answered questions about it for an hour and a half. On 15 Nov she answered a member's request to explain why Nvidia sells cards with part of their memory switched off. The digest counts 28 question-and-answer pairs from 23 askers; a good part of those are arguments and are left off. The card lists 9 of her replies with the post each one answered.

candidate.source: The digest's Interview material (sections.interview), second of five. One of the four pairs the digest prints is on this card (the Nvidia question).

checks.windowPosts: Read her 29 top-level posts and all of her replies to other people's questions that the data holds (29, of which 6 are in flagged stories or carry a sensitivity mark). Several threads are arguments with people opposed to AI, one is an exchange about being misgendered, and several posts are about the outages the digest flags. None of that is on the card. No post asks not to be quoted.

didInWindow: Posted lists of security advisories in open-source projects (13 and 18 Nov), thanked the maintainers, and linked her write-up "Property Testing with Agent Swarms" (recursion.wtf/posts/agents-and-property-tests). Posted a cyberdeck design on 19 Nov: a small stand holding a split keyboard with a trackball in the middle, around a phone or tablet used as a terminal; she said it follows published CAD drawings and that the hardware was already in the mail.
couldBeShown: The cyberdeck post (19 Nov) has an image. No alt text in the data; the researcher has not seen it. Her words for it: "a small kiosk mounting ZSA Voyager split keyboards with a center trackball reachable using both hands".
The advisories are public pages on github.com (linked from her posts of 13 and 18 Nov), and her write-up is a public page. The researcher has not opened them.

notUnderstood: I have not seen the cyberdeck image. "luna" and "astra" in the "guardrails" answer are model names as far as the surrounding posts show. The "lil guy" link goes to a page titled "Snowball" on an Overwatch wiki; I take it to be a small robot character and have not checked. Two pairs the digest prints were left out because I could not follow them: a member's question about a short name for a comic panel (smbc "aaaah"), which seems to be about people's reactions to the outage, and a question "How do you do this" whose subject is not in the data.
leftOut: Three of the four pairs the digest prints: one is in a flagged story, one is a retort in an argument, one I did not understand. Her exchanges with people opposed to AI (15 to 17 Nov), an exchange about her pronouns (14 Nov), replies about the outages and about a public figure's affair, a post about a tattoo and a day off, and a post about her ears. A long reply about druids in a role-playing game thread started by an account with 20,635 followers outside the cluster.
sensitive: Part of her week is conflict: arguments with people opposed to AI, and a thread in which she was misgendered. Those are out of bounds (identity, interpersonal conflict) and none is on the card, but the screen should know the week had them. Security advisories are disclosures made with the maintainers' thanks, not legal trouble; still, nothing should suggest she attacked anyone's software. The asker of the Nvidia question spoke in the previous episode. One asker is a small account (111 followers). The Nvidia thread starts from a post that quotes a write-up of a hardware exploit and carries a "health" keyword mark on the quoted post; the quoted post is not on the card.
